clue.text: A tax from which the metropolis benefits

definitions.meaning: the levy charged on profit made by selling an asset that has risen in value
read literally, the profits that the capital city collects

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: the capital (the metropolis) gains, i.e. benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: The levy is named after the profits it is charged on; the phrase also reads as advantages accruing to a capital city.

clue.text: The guilty priest I admitted into sect

indicators.note: admitted into says the next pieces are let inside the word for a sect

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: A guilty clergyman has been taken into a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted into' puts PR and I inside CULT. 'The guilty' stands for the guilty party.
explanation.definitionFit: The offender is the person responsible for a wrongdoing, the party found to blame.

clue.text: Unknown number from Cornish resort making reparation

indicators.note: from says the unknown number is taken out of the resort's name

parts.note: Penzance is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities, so Z is an unknown number

explanation.surface: A mystery figure leaves a Cornish seaside town to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes Z from PENZANCE. 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of atonement is offered to make up for a wrong, which is what reparation is.

clue.text: Get-up in which seaman appears for a change

indicators.note: in which ... appears says the sailor stands inside the word for a get-up

parts.note: a turnout is a person's outfit or get-up
AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor turns up in some outfit just to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts AB inside TURNOUT; 'appears for' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of position or opinion is a complete change of direction.

clue.text: I get cold in French bed, but that's allowable

indicators.note: in says the I and the cold letter are put inside the French word for bed

parts.note: lit is French for bed
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone shivers in a French bed but insists it is quite permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and C inside LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lawful or permitted is acceptable under the rules.

clue.text: A sober man is an oddity, but reaches his goal

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who never drinks alcohol

indicators.note: oddity says the two words before it are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is a curiosity, yet he still achieves what he set out to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddity' rearranges IS AN into AINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Achieves or arrives at an aim, which is reaching one's target.

clue.text: Fellow-member upset by Japanese drama

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned over and read from the bottom

parts.note: MPs call a colleague 'the hon. member', hon. being short for honourable

explanation.surface: A colleague is distressed by a piece of Japanese theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HON over. In the British Parliament members refer to one another as 'the Honourable Member'.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical form of masked theatre from Japan, dating from the fourteenth century.

clue.text: Audience for cad's performance is in a dicey situation

parts.note: the house is the audience in a theatre

indicators.note: a performance here is a carry-on, a fuss, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre crowd turns up to watch a scoundrel's show, which is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges FOR CADS into OFCARDS. 'is in' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy structure that could collapse at any moment, so a precarious state of affairs.

clue.text: Bird cry in the east end

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: a howl is a loud cry

explanation.surface: A bird calls out somewhere in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the east end' drops the H of HOWL, as a Cockney (a native of London's East End) would.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird of prey with large eyes and a hooting call.

clue.text: TUC chap ordered to clear backlog

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are rearranged, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A trade union official is told to deal with a pile of outstanding work.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress. 'ordered' looks like a command to the chap but rearranges his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring outstanding work up to date is to deal with what has piled up.

clue.text: Debating query on the reason for discipline

definitions.meaning: a question raised in a formal meeting about whether proceedings follow the rules
read literally, the purpose of keeping order

explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the link between the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedural objection raised in a debate; also, literally, the purpose behind keeping things orderly.

clue.text: Plant it's no good planting in the country

indicators.note: planting in says the letters for no good are set inside the country

parts.note: Syria is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that it is useless trying to grow anything in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside but is a nation; 'planting in' puts NG inside SYRIA. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub genus that includes lilac and the mock orange.

clue.text: Tour oil refinery in the Lebanon

parts.note: a trip is a tour or outing

indicators.note: a refinery processes oil, so the word oil is reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A visit to an oil refinery in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refinery' rearranges OIL into OLI. The definition is a place found in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in northern Lebanon shares its name with the Libyan capital.

clue.text: Fantastic piece of trout, really

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An angler marvels at a truly wonderful bit of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or unconventional, beyond the bounds of the usual.

clue.text: On view? There's some mistake

parts.note: over can mean on, as in a cloth laid over a table
a sight is a view

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is on display and is told an error has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's some' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: An error caused by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Fan acquires outdated farming vehicle

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
a tractor pulls ploughs and trailers on a farm

explanation.surface: An enthusiast buys an old farm machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an enthusiast but is a ventilating fan; 'acquires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or bathroom ventilator that draws out stale air.

clue.text: Firm gets fresh update about time for take-over

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the time letter
fresh says the word update is made anew, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A company issues new information about the timing of an acquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges UPDATE and 'about' wraps it round T, giving UPDETAT after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden seizure of government power, a takeover by force.

clue.text: See GP grab one and three-quarters

indicators.note: grab says the doctor takes hold of the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, informally a doc
I is the Roman numeral for one
E, S and E are three points of the compass, the quarters

explanation.surface: Watch the family doctor seize a portion and a bit more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grab' puts I inside DOC. 'quarters' are compass points, so three of them give ESE; 'See' is a bishop's see, not look.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under his authority.

clue.text: A backward buffoon of unsociable nature

indicators.note: backward says the word for buffoon is read in reverse

parts.note: a fool is a buffoon

explanation.surface: A slow-witted clown keeps himself to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like a description of the buffoon's wits but turns FOOL around into LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant and reserved, keeping away from company.

clue.text: A familiar Frenchman in unesco, maybe

parts.note: a familiar is a close friend, a crony
M. is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A friendly Frenchman works at the United Nations agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. UNESCO is formed from the initials of United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization.
explanation.definitionFit: Initials pronounced as a word form an abbreviation of this type; 'maybe' marks an example.

clue.text: Not in business with me as a result

parts.note: out means not at home, not in
Co. is short for company, a business
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being away from work leaves me with consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: The consequence or end product of an action.

clue.text: Leftist rebelled on seeing new labour's symbol

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
rose, as in rose up, means rebelled

explanation.surface: A left-winger revolted when the party's modernised emblem was unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on seeing' is link wording. The British Labour Party, rebranded as New Labour under Tony Blair, uses this flower as its emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Labour Party's emblem is a flower of this colour.

clue.text: Quite unbowed before going to court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone stands tall and proud before appearing at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing perfectly upright, with no stoop at all.

clue.text: Arab takes time to produce air-purifier

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Arab takes time to produce air-purifier' (7): AERATOR parses as A + TOR round ERA (time), but no clue word gives A TOR; 'Arab' looks garbled and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Arab takes time to produce air-purifier

clue.text: Hide in covert enclave, initially

parts.note: covert means secret

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of enclave is used

explanation.surface: Go into hiding in a secret enclave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'Hide' is a verb here, to conceal.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal or stash away out of sight.

clue.text: Sounds like it's fish for tea

indicators.note: Sounds like says the word for the fish is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Someone claims fish is what's served for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CHAR and CHA sound alike; both are slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is an informal British word for a cuppa, from the Chinese.

clue.text: Love, you and I are in queer street

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
we means you and I together

explanation.surface: Darling, the two of us are in a strange road.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer Street is old British slang for being in debt or financial trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in debt, to be indebted to someone.

clue.text: Rest assured you're welcome to what's mine

definitions.meaning: you can believe what I say, trust me
read literally, an offer to remove one's possessions

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning believe me; also, literally, an invitation to help oneself to my property.
